messages:
melanie: heads-up — noticed a perf regression after pushing CUDA driver 545.23 to us-west-2 dedicated pool. p95 for short sequences (<128 tokens) jumped ~10% and we're seeing tail latency spikes. initial profiling points to a different attention kernel being selected (warp-optimized -> mem-heavy path).

bench-bot: repro runs on bench-1 confirm the regression. quick profile snippet below: 
```
# perf counters (sample)
kernel chosen: attn_mem_v1 (prev: attn_warp_v2)
avg token latency (seq=64): 1.24ms -> 1.37ms (+10.5%)
sm_efficiency: 87% -> 71%
dram_read_bw: 420GB/s -> 560GB/s
kv_cache_misses: 0.9% -> 4.6%
```

priya: hm — looks like the autotuner's microbench opted for the mem-bound kernel after the driver changed scheduling/occupancy behavior. the autotune probe harness was using `--seq 512` by default, so short sequences were under-represented.

tj: checked autotune logs — tie-break logic moved toward measured_throughput numbers rather than latency for the short-seq regime. the harness reports higher throughput for attn_mem_v1 at long seqs on the new driver, so the heuristic flipped.

devon: that matches. we also see more KV-cache churn because the mem path has larger ephemeral working set; combined with our batching_prefetch=4 it's evicting cached blocks for concurrent low-latency requests.

melanie: proposed immediate mitigations: 
1) runtime override: add per-model kernel_hint to prefer attn_warp_v2 for seq <= 256
2) tweak batching: prefer small-batch low-latency path for kv_cache_hit traffic (reduce prefetch)
3) infra option: rollback driver on a canary nodepool while we validate fixes

ops-bot: can schedule driver rollback canary. sample pin command:
```
./infra/drivers/pin_driver.sh --region us-west-2 --nodeset dedicated-canary --driver 543.11
```

priya: for a fast runtime mitigation i can push a dynamic override: `runtime.KERNEL_OVERRIDE=attn_warp_v2:seq<=256`. will do a canary deploy to dedicated-canary routing.

tj: pushed the routing hotfix to canary. quick smoke test (force seq_hint=64):
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $X" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"hi","seq_hint":64}' \
  https://dedicated-canary.redwood/api/v1/infer | jq .meta.kernel
# expected: attn_warp_v2
```

bench-bot: canary results after override: 
```
avg token latency (seq=64): 0.78ms -> 0.70ms (improved vs prod)
p95: 1.12ms -> 1.02ms
kv_cache_miss_rate: 3.8% -> 1.1%
```

devon: nice — that suggests kernel choice is the main lever. next steps: 
- telemetry: emit kernel_pick and seq_len for every request for 72h
- autotune: change probe distro to include 0-256-heavy samples and re-run on CI GPUs
- ops: rollback driver on remaining affected nodes if canary stable

melanie: also flagging KV cache interaction: attn_mem_v1 increases per-layer working set which, combined with our prefetching, causes extra evictions for short, low-latency flows. short-term tweak: reduce `batching.prefetch_limit` from 4 -> 2 for p99-sensitive models.

priya: i'll add a config toggle `batching.prefetch_limit` and gate it behind a devexp rollout. pushing patch for canary now.

tj: filed a revert ticket for the driver upgrade so infra has org awareness. fallback routing plan: route short-seq traffic to hosted pool if rollback needs time.

devon: also updating autotune harness to include microbench runs: `autotune_probe --seq 16 --seq 32 --seq 64 --seq 128` and to weight probes by prod seq histogram. this should avoid undersampling short paths.

melanie: thanks — action items assigned. we'll monitor canary and reconvene in 2h with telemetry. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: scheduled task: driver-pin job queued for dedicated-canary at 2032104625
